Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, we can conclude that granulomatous myelotoxicity and enteritis developed in a 21-year-old female within 3 weeks of initiating sulfasalazine for rheumatoid arthritis. Following a short course of corticosteroids, the patient had resolution of her cholestatic hepatitis, rash, eosinophilia, and gastrointestinal symptoms with no residual manifestations at 7 months follow-up.

This information suggests that it is likely Crohn's disease, as the development of enteritis and granulomatous inflammation in response to sulfasalazine and corticosteroids aligns with the known pathophysiology of the condition. Additionally, the resolution of cholestatic hepatitis and other symptoms indicates a successful treatment outcome.

It is worth noting that while Crohn's disease can cause a wide range of gastrointestinal symptoms, granulomatous myelotoxicity and enteritis are specific manifestations of the condition. Therefore, this information provides strong evidence to support the diagnosis of Crohn's disease.
